newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Yadav asks ministers not to quit-PTI.
newsitem.headline: India's Yadav asks ministers not to quit-PTI.

text.p: Laloo Prasad Yadav, leader of India's Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) party, changed his mind on a demand made earlier on Friday and asked three supporters in Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's cabinet not to resign, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

The news agency said the decision followed a statement in Madras made by the president of the regional Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), Muthuvel Karunanidhi, that the ruling United Front coalition had not yet decided on whether to admit the RJD.
Karunanidhi said the Steering Committee of the United Front would decide at a meeting on July 25 whether to admit the RJD, which broke away from Gujral's Janata Dal party on July 5.

The DMK has been opposing a move by the Communist Party of India-Marxist to keep the RJD out of the coalition, saying this would weaken the coalition and help the rival Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

The communists wanted the RJD out of the alliance because Yadav has refused to resign as chief minister of the state of Bihar after federal police indicted him in a $280 million embezzlement scandal. Yadav says he is innocent.

The DMK, upset with the communists, threatened on Monday to pull its ministers out of Gujral's cabinet, saying some coalition partners had compromised on the alliance's dignity and a shared programme by forcing in their hard line on others.
